parsed.explanation: The key lemma — that for every term x the small-prime trace σ(x) is good — is exactly ledger statement L6.2, and its entire proof reads "Induction over the sequence terms in increasing order (standard; details omitted)." No argument for all terms appears anywhere: Section 4 of the falsification notes only gestures at a construction "Rp^k" without proving the resulting number lies in [A,x) and is itself a term, and the final section explicitly labels its 19,585-term check "Computational evidence (not used as proof)". Hence L6.2 is unestablished as written despite the "complete" status line; supplying the induction is a lemma-sized repair.
